item.title: US shoppers tighten budgets, but still find room for treats and splurges
item.description: Walmart's disappointing sales and Home Depot's strength among budget-conscious do-it-yourselfers indicate middle-class American consumers are growing more tight-fisted, even as wealthier shoppers have kept supporting luxury brands like Ralph Lauren.
item.dc:creator: Juveria Tabassum, Anuja Mistry
item.content:encoded: Walmart's disappointing sales and Home Depot's strength among budget-conscious do-it-yourselfers indicate middle-class American consumers are growing more tight-fisted, even as wealthier shoppers have kept supporting luxury brands like Ralph Lauren. Earnings reports over the past month from a slate of U.S. supermarkets, home improvement stores, restaurants and luxury brands have shown consumers directing most of their spending toward essentials and putting off big projects, while still making room for affordable treats and occasional splurges. While affluent shoppers continue to snap up Ralph Lauren (RL.N) linen shorts and prestige beauty products, lower-income consumers are stretching budgets at Taco Bell and Ross Stores (ROST.O) , pairing value meals and discount apparel with essential purchases. Aggregate spending has not collapsed, but "households are becoming much more deliberate about where their money goes," said Lale Akoner, global market strategist at eToro. In an era of [USN:S0N42N01Y TEXT:"elevated gasoline prices"], the trend is expected to carry into the key holiday shopping season. Retailers will probably rely on a mix of discounts, new merchandise and higher-end brands to keep customers coming. "When fuel prices increase and get above $4, perhaps there's a psychological impact to that ... consumers are making trade-offs," Walmart CFO John David Rainey said on Thursday after the company reported its slowest [USN:L6N44H0NR TEXT:"same-store sales growth"] in six years despite rolling back prices on 11,000 items. Price cuts alone may no longer be enough to compel a reticent shopper. At McDonald's (MCD.N) , discounted meal options this quarter in an otherwise expensive menu [USN:L4N4440UH TEXT:"failed to draw"] customers, who responded more strongly to fresh menu items at [USN:L6N43V1HB TEXT:"Yum Brands YUM.N"] stores such as Taco Bell, KFC and Pizza Hut. Walmart, TJ Maxx owner TJX and Home Depot all warned this week that shoppers remain [USN:L6N43I08L TEXT:""selective""] while [USN:L1N44A133 TEXT:"U.S. retail sales"] in July logged their first fall in nine months. "Selectivity is visible in snacks and impulse, where the shopper will still pay up for the one item they came in wanting and skip the second one," said Joel Goldstein, president at Mr. Checkout Distributors. PRICE CUTS AND PRICEY BRANDS Companies known for affordable luxury including [USN:L4N4491DH TEXT:"Tapestry TPR.N "], [USN:L4N44G0PR TEXT:"Estee Lauder"] (EL.N) and [USN:L6N44A0LX TEXT:"Birkenstock BIRK.N "] reported strong results on demand for apparel, bags, and fragrances priced well above $100. Coffee chain Starbucks (SBUX.O) has managed to [USN:L6N43V1BH TEXT:"recover sales"] for its pricey lattes as consumers rewarded improved service times and a better store environment. Catering to both ends of the economy, retailers are combining price cuts with stocking higher-end labels. Target, for example, is [USN:L6N44G147 TEXT:"expanding its private label"] food brand Good & Gather while stocking [USN:L4N41X1IX TEXT:"premium items"] like Bugaboo baby strollers. It also priced about 95% of its back-to-school supplies around or below last year's levels. Target as well as Walmart are putting back money received from sizable tariff refunds into [USN:L4N44F12R TEXT:"lowering prices"] on pantry staples such as beef, which became costly over the past year, partly due to the import duties. But discounts have their limits. "For more stretched consumers, lower prices can only go so far when household budgets are already under pressure. The constraint is increasingly how much disposable income they have left to spend at all," said Axel Rudolph, chief technical analyst at IG Group. Even Walmart, which raised its annual outlook, said its [USN:L4N42Q17S TEXT:"back-to-school"] shopping season got off to a good start due to the presence of "more elevated brands" and "more expensive merchandise" that appeal to a broader range of shoppers. MORE SUPERMARKET TRIPS, LESS SPENDING One of the clearest signs of consumer caution emerged in basket sizes at Walmart and Target, where shoppers continued to visit stores but spent less per trip. "Even Walmart, which has been supported by more affluent households trading down, isn't able to keep average spending growth rising," said Angeline Ong, senior investment analyst at IG Group. The same caution is weighing on home improvement retailers. [USN:L4N44F0G4 TEXT:"Home Depot"] and [USN:L4N44G0QR TEXT:"Lowe's"] benefited from demand for maintenance and seasonal projects, but higher borrowing costs had consumers continuing to postpone larger renovations that typically require financing. "The real challenge would be if there's also a decline in traffic," said Brian Jacobsen, chief economic strategist at Annex Wealth Management. "That could happen if there isn't some relief on budgets from higher rates and high gasoline prices."

item.title: Washington IndyCar race touted by Trump draws Boeing, Starlink, Delta as new sponsors
item.description: Several major companies will be sponsoring an IndyCar race for the first time when the Freedom 250 Grand Prix, touted by President Donald Trump, takes place around Washington, D.C., on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: David Shepardson
item.content:encoded: Several major companies will be sponsoring an IndyCar race for the first time when the Freedom 250 Grand Prix, touted by President Donald Trump, takes place around Washington, D.C., on Sunday. New backers include Boeing (BA.N) , SpaceX's (SPCX.O) Starlink and Delta Air Lines (DAL.N) , Bud Denker, the chair of the 250-mile (402-km) race and president of Penske Corp, said at a press conference on Thursday. Penske is running the event. The event will cap off a series of celebrations of the 250th anniversary of U.S. independence. "I love the race," Trump said when he signed the executive order calling for the race in January. Trump will wave the green flag at the start of the race and take a lap around the course in the presidential limousine. Trump is expected to invite some executives to watch the race with him in a special suite, three sources said. Many of the companies will have corporate suites along the race course. The event has dozens of corporate sponsors, allowing executives to mingle with the many administration officials and lawmakers expected to be at the race. "This is also an opportunity for us to grow our sport and, by showcasing it to these companies that were never part of our sport," Denker said. IndyCar’s Freedom 250 Grand Prix will involve drivers hitting speeds of 170 miles per hour (274 kph) on historic Pennsylvania Avenue, around the National Archives and through some of the country’s cultural institutions on Saturday and Sunday. Denker said Delta CEO Ed Bastian will attend. Other companies sponsoring the event include General Motors (GM.N) , Honda (7267.T) , United Airlines (UAL.O) , Amazon.com's (AMZN.O) AWS unit, Shell (SHEL.L) , Gulfstream, Altria (MO.N) , Verizon (VZ.N) and Washington Gas. Many senior executives and members of Congress are expected to be on hand, the sources said. The White House referred questions about Trump's plans for the race to Penske. Washington Mayor Muriel Bowser said the city expects 140,000 people to attend race events each day. A large swath of downtown will close to traffic.

item.title: Tankers stack up as Venezuela sells oil faster than its ports can handle
item.description: Venezuela's dilapidated oil port terminals are imposing a de facto export cap on the country's resurgent crude production, with tankers having to wait up to 30 days to load because of ageing infrastructure, power outages and quality issues, according to shipping data, sources and documents.
item.dc:creator: Marianna Parraga
item.content:encoded: Venezuela's dilapidated oil port terminals are imposing a de facto export cap on the country's resurgent crude production, with tankers having to wait up to 30 days to load because of ageing infrastructure, power outages and quality issues, according to shipping data, sources and documents. The delays are putting roadblocks on a U.S. plan to quickly boost Venezuela's oil exports following a flagship pact with global trading houses. The fight for infrastructure looks likely to intensify as many partners of state energy firm PDVSA get ready to market their share of output independently under new contract terms. The last time Venezuela's oil customers had to deal with such long delays was during a naval blockade imposed by the U.S. on the South American country late last year, part of a strategy that culminated with the January 3 capture of then-President Nicolas Maduro. Since then, interim leader Delcy Rodriguez has been sticking to Washington's plan to reanimate oil exports. But in recent months, PDVSA and its partners have been unable to [USN:L1N4400P6 TEXT:"surpass"] 1.25 million barrels per day of exports even amid rising crude output, stock drainage and high global demand, vessel monitoring data showed. When output peaked at more than 3 million bpd more than two decades ago, the nation's terminals were able to handle over 2.5 million bpd of exports, with vessels getting in and out of Venezuelan waters in less than a week. The loading hiccups are triggering disputes over demurrage, crude quality and ship contamination, according to maritime documents, four sources and vessel monitoring data. "The speed of crude transfers from tanks to vessels is incredibly slow, which forces tankers to occupy docks for longer than their assigned loading windows. And if a ship arrives to discharge imports, it takes even longer due to lack of fuel storage capacity," a PDVSA source said. Venezuela's oil ministry and PDVSA did not reply to requests for comment. The delays are visible in the dozens of tankers that swirl waiting for oil cargoes at the country's anchorages, particularly near the Jose port on Venezuela's northeastern coast, which handles about 70% of the country's overall exports. Company shipping reports seen by Reuters showed interruptions this year due to equipment malfunctions, quality issues and power outages when loading and unloading at Jose. Even companies in more privileged positions to use docks after decades of partnership with PDVSA, like U.S. oil major Chevron (CVX.N) , are looking for solutions to improve loading, including requesting access to ports so far dedicated to domestic shipping, sources said. Chevron did not reply to a request for comment. Venezuela's oil export [USN:L1N3Y70PH TEXT:"agreement"] with the U.S., extended several times, has allowed traders including Vitol and Trafigura to ship over 140 million barrels of crude and fuel this year, with most cargoes bound to the U.S. and others re-entering markets that had not seen Venezuelan barrels for years, such as Europe and India, as U.S. sanctions are eased. But as Washington pushes a $100 billion energy reconstruction plan in Venezuela that is mainly focused on boosting crude output, midstream and downstream projects – including those to repair terminals and [USN:L1N4290ZZ TEXT:"refineries"] – are not being prioritized. U.S. and Venezuelan officials praised the oil export recovery in two conferences in Houston this week, and acknowledged infrastructure challenges they said can be addressed through fresh investment. "We are today in a phase of recovery, but the infrastructure is there," said PDVSA's vice president Jovanny Martinez at one of the conferences. "There are deficiencies and reliability must improve." BETWEEN RUST AND LEAKS The traffic jam at the Jose and neighboring Pozuelos anchorages partly predates the current export boom. Venezuela's oil docks are cluttered with relics of the years in which the country was under severe U.S. sanctions, such as blacklisted tankers that arrived quietly and have been unable to leave. One of them, flying a false Guyanese flag, is docked at PDVSA's Guaraguao port in Puerto La Cruz, its hull and deck visibly rusty even from a distance. Once known as Syrma and used to transport oil to Cuba before being renamed Consul, it has remained there for two years sheltering from a U.S. crackdown on dark fleets that brought seizures and arrests, shipping data and maritime databases showed. Like many others, the vessel is occupying berth space now at a premium, even as foreign companies seek to reactivate idled terminals to expand crude exports. In mid-August, only two of Guaraguao's seven docks were fully in service, a worker from the terminal said. The competition for port capacity has prompted many customers to resort to terminals and ship-to-ship transfer areas where oil leaks that stain their tankers' hulls are frequent, causing additional delays and costs, according to the sources and documents. PDVSA, meanwhile, is increasingly being charged thousands of dollars for demurrage — a delay surcharge applied for each day a tanker remains waiting beyond its assigned loading window — which it has agreed to pay only in crude. The state company is requiring new customers to pay for cargoes at delivery without any form of credit, which complicates invoicing if those customers claim surcharges or quality-related price discounts, the sources added. The migration of dozens of oil contracts to new terms approved in a sweeping [USN:L1N3YU13L TEXT:"energy reform"] that took effect in late July is expected to exacerbate the fight for infrastructure. But PDVSA has made clear, the sources said, that it will keep control of its terminals, including all cargo scheduling, at least for now.

item.title: Irán promete una respuesta "devastadora" ante las amenazas de EEUU
item.description: Irán afirmó el viernes que su respuesta a cualquier nueva amenaza de Estados Unidos sería "devastadora", después de que Washington se comprometiera a imponer las sanciones financieras más duras de la historia con el objetivo de derrocar al liderazgo iraní.
item.dc:creator: Jana Choukeir, Susan Heavey
item.content:encoded: Irán afirmó el viernes que su respuesta a cualquier nueva amenaza de Estados Unidos sería "devastadora", después de que Washington se comprometiera a imponer las sanciones financieras más duras de la historia con el objetivo de derrocar al liderazgo iraní. Las [USN:L6N44H0ZU TEXT:"declaraciones"][USN:L6N44H0ZU TEXT:" del secretario del Tesoro de EEUU"], Scott Bessent, el jueves ocurrieron tras una advertencia del presidente Donald Trump sobre las consecuencias económicas que sufriría cualquier país que proporcionara "cualquier tipo de ayuda vital a Irán". Bessent prometió dar más detalles el lunes. El jefe del Estado Mayor de las Fuerzas Armadas de Irán, el general de división Ali Abdollahi, dijo que la reacción de la República Islámica sería amplia y decisiva. "Con su preparación en tierra, mar, aire, defensa aérea y ciberespacio, las Fuerzas Armadas de Irán responderán a las nuevas amenazas del enemigo con respuestas aplastantes, punitivas y devastadoras", dijo Abdollahi según recogen medios iraníes. El influyente presidente del Parlamento iraní, Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf, principal negociador del país en las conversaciones mediadas con Estados Unidos, dijo que Washington parecía haber llegado a la conclusión de que no podría imponerse en un enfrentamiento militar directo. "Debemos elaborar planes para hacer frente a las sanciones injustas, de modo que podamos superarlas", dijo durante una visita al vecino Irak, acusando a EEUU e Israel de recurrir a lo que calificó de guerra económica y "cognitiva". BESSENT DICE QUE LAS MEDIDAS NO DEBERÍAN HACER SUBIR EL PRECIO DEL PETRÓLEO Los precios del petróleo se estabilizaban el viernes, pero se encaminaban hacia una segunda subida semanal debido a la preocupación por las exportaciones energéticas del golfo Pérsico. El petróleo alcanzó el jueves su máximo en más de tres semanas tras la amenaza de sanciones, destinada a obligar a Irán a aceptar el fin de un conflicto que ha dejado bloqueados millones de barriles de petróleo de Oriente Medio. "No estoy seguro de por qué el petróleo ha subido de repente por esto", declaró Bessent a la CNBC. "Si estamos ejerciendo la máxima presión económica, eso significa que probablemente no habrá una reanudación cinética a gran escala", dijo, utilizando un término que hace referencia a la fuerza militar. Miles de personas han perdido la vida en esta guerra, que ha arrastrado los países del golfo Pérsico y ha conmocionado a los mercados al demostrar Irán su capacidad para restringir el tráfico marítimo a través del estrecho de Ormuz, una vía navegable por la que circulaba aproximadamente una quinta parte de todo el petróleo comercializado antes de febrero. Estados Unidos e Irán han anunciado en dos ocasiones acuerdos de alto el fuego, en abril y en junio, con el objetivo de restablecer la libre circulación del tráfico marítimo a través de Ormuz como paso previo para poner fin al conflicto, que ya dura casi seis meses, pero ambos acuerdos se desmoronaron rápidamente. Irán ha soportado sanciones económicas casi continuas y severas durante casi 50 años, desde la Revolución Islámica de 1979. Antes de que Bessent tomara la palabra, el Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores de Irán dijo que condenaba las sanciones económicas y comerciales de EEUU, calificándolas de "terrorismo económico" que no "provocaría ni la más mínima vacilación en la determinación de los iraníes de salvaguardar la independencia, la dignidad y la soberanía nacional de Irán". Bessent dijo a la CNBC que daría más detalles sobre el último paquete de medidas y que "hablaría exactamente de lo que vamos a hacer" con respecto a Irán en una rueda de prensa el lunes. "Es un doble golpe. Tenemos el bloqueo (sobre Irán) y vamos a aplicar las sanciones más duras de la historia", añadió, refiriéndose al bloqueo naval estadounidense impuesto a Irán en abril y suspendido durante un mes a mediados de junio. "Va a funcionar en Irán y vamos a derrumbar este régimen. Es hora de que nuestros aliados y el resto del mundo tomen una decisión", afirmó. Trump se encuentra bajo presión en su propio país para poner fin a la guerra, ya que los elevados precios del combustible están lastrando sus índices de popularidad y podrían poner en peligro el control del Congreso por parte de su Partido Republicano en las elecciones de mitad de legislatura de noviembre. EL BLOQUEO REIMPUESTO POR EEUU EMPIEZA A REDUCIR LOS FLUJOS DE PETRÓLEO HACIA CHINA China compra más del 80% del petróleo exportado por Irán, según datos de 2025 de la empresa de análisis Kpler, pero enzarzarse en una mayor guerra económica con Pekín —uno de los principales exportadores a EEUU, incluso de minerales de tierras raras de vital importancia— conlleva el riesgo de represalias contra Washington. Cuando se le preguntó si Estados Unidos podría tomar medidas contra China por hacer negocios con Irán, Bessent respondió que era mejor mantener muchas conversaciones en privado. "Hay que tener en cuenta que los chinos obtienen el 50% (de su) energía (...) del golfo Pérsico. Por lo tanto, les vendría muy bien sumarse a la iniciativa", afirmó. La embajada de China en Washington declaró que "las sanciones y la presión no ayudan a resolver el problema". "China insta a las partes implicadas a actuar de forma responsable y a resolver la cuestión por la vía política y diplomática", según un portavoz de la embajada. Las ofertas de crudo iraní a los compradores chinos [USN:L6N44I0L9 TEXT:"ya han disminuido"] y los precios se han disparado esta semana, ya que el bloqueo estadounidense de los puertos iraníes —reimpuesto el 13 de julio— ha reducido los envíos de Teherán, según informaron fuentes del sector a Reuters.

item.title: Monte dei Paschi di Siena presenta una oferta por BPM y Banca Generali para frenar la opa de Intesa
item.description: El banco italiano Monte dei Paschi di Siena lanzó el viernes sendas ofertas de adquisición simultáneas e independientes, íntegramente en acciones y valoradas en unos 34.000 millones de euros (39.800 millones de dólares) en total, por su competidor Banco BPM y la gestora de patrimonios Banca Generali , lo que intensifica la batalla que está reconfigurando el sector bancario italiano.
item.dc:creator: Valentina Za, Andrea Mandala, Giulio Piovaccari
item.content:encoded: El banco italiano Monte dei Paschi di Siena (BMPS.MI) lanzó el viernes sendas ofertas de adquisición simultáneas e independientes, íntegramente en acciones y valoradas en unos 34.000 millones de euros (39.800 millones de dólares) en total, por su competidor Banco BPM (BAMI.MI) y la gestora de patrimonios Banca Generali (BGN.MI) , lo que intensifica la batalla que está reconfigurando el sector bancario italiano. Las ofertas son la respuesta del consejero delegado, Luigi Lovaglio, a la opa hostil de 36.000 millones de euros lanzada en junio por Intesa Sanpaolo (ISP.MI) , líder del sector, que ha suscitado preocupación en Roma por una posible reducción de la competencia en la banca nacional. MPS también propuso una "distribución extraordinaria" a sus accionistas por valor de 4.000 millones de euros, frente a los 3.000 millones en efectivo ofrecidos por Intesa. El dividendo de MPS se realizaría en parte en efectivo y en parte mediante acciones de Generali (GASI.MI) , equivalentes a alrededor del 4,5% de la aseguradora italiana, en la que MPS posee una participación del 13,3% a través del banco de inversión Mediobanca (MDBI.MI) , adquirido el año pasado. El anuncio no convencía a los inversores en la apertura del mercado: mientras las acciones de MPS subían un 0,7% a las 0820 GMT, las de Banco BPM y Banca Generali caían un 0,7% y un 1,8%, respectivamente. Tanto Banco BPM como Banca Generali declinaron hacer comentarios. MPS ya había explorado una posible operación con Banco BPM para frustrar la adquisición por parte de Intesa, pero ambos bancos pusieron fin a las conversaciones el mes pasado después de que el principal inversor de BPM, el francés Crédit Agricole , expresara su rechazo al plan. MPS es el "socio natural para una integración amistosa", dijo Lovaglio al presentar el plan, cuyo objetivo es crear el tercer mayor banco de Italia por activos. El nuevo grupo se situaría además entre los 10 mayores bancos de Europa, añadió. (1 dólar = 0,8553 euros)

item.title: India's ICICI Bank doubles overseas borrowing limit to $5 billion
item.description: India's ICICI Bank said on Friday its board approved doubling the limit for overseas borrowings to $5 billion, as the country's second-largest private lender ramps up fundraising in international markets.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: India's ICICI Bank (ICBK.NS) said on Friday its board approved doubling the limit for overseas borrowings to $5 billion, as the country's second-largest private lender ramps up fundraising in international markets. Indian banks have accelerated overseas fundraising after the Reserve Bank of India brought forward the closure of a foreign-exchange swap facility to August 31 from the end of September. Private and state-run lenders were on track to raise at least $5 billion through dollar bonds and loans, [USN:L4N44E0JA TEXT:"bankers told Reuters"] earlier this week. ICICI Bank has [USN:L4N44F04P TEXT:"already raised"] $2.05 billion through dollar debt in the past month, the most among Indian banks since the RBI announced the swap window in early June. Earlier this week, ICICI Bank raised $750 million through five-year dollar bonds, its third dollar fundraising in a month, two merchant bankers told Reuters on Tuesday.

item.title: Mourinho returns with calm words and hard edge as Real reset begins
item.description: Jose Mourinho walked into his first Real Madrid press conference three minutes early on Friday, but the message was deliberate: commitment is non-negotiable, competition is unavoidable and frustration over selection decisions will not be tolerated.
item.dc:creator: Fernando Kallas
item.content:encoded: Jose Mourinho walked into his first Real Madrid press conference three minutes early on Friday, but the message was deliberate: commitment is non-negotiable, competition is unavoidable and frustration over selection decisions will not be tolerated. Three days after his formal unveiling [USN:L6N44F0XI TEXT:"behind closed doors"], Mourinho faced the media at Real's Valdebebas training complex before Saturday's [USN:L6N4480IL TEXT:"LaLiga opener at Espanyol"], speaking for more than 40 minutes in a notably measured tone. Despite Real entering the season after back-to-back trophyless campaigns and with pressure mounting on President Florentino Perez, who recently secured re-election, Mourinho rejected the idea that the club was gripped by anxiety. Instead, he said the mood was one of anticipation. "We are tired of playing friendlies. We don't love football because of friendlies, we are all eager to jump right back into competitive football," Mourinho said. "I wouldn't say the feeling here is pressure... It's more like adrenaline. Which is positive, that pump. I don't feel pressure. Because I have a lot of confidence in the work we've put in and in the players' hunger, commitment." COLLECTIVE RESPONSIBILITY Mourinho repeatedly stressed the importance of collective responsibility in a squad packed with elite talent, while making clear that individual ambitions must come second to the team. "What we need is to not negotiate things that are non-negotiable. Commitment is mandatory," he said. "The team must go ahead of personal feelings. Tomorrow will be the first time the players will have to deal with it. I can't start a match with 15 players. "I don't want easy decisions, that would be benching a player who got frustrated because he didn't play what he thought he would. I want to make hard decisions, want players that don't fall into the trap of frustration. I want players who work harder to earn a spot in the team." Mourinho also addressed the challenge of accommodating Kylian Mbappe, Jude Bellingham and Vinicius Jr in the same side while maintaining balance. "I don't think these positions are incompatible; I'm very confident we're going to have a great season," Mourinho said. "It's obvious that I can't build the team around each of them like Brazil do with Vini, France with Mbappe and England with Bellingham. It's harder for me to find a place for all three of them, but that's where we are." STARTING FROM SCRATCH Mourinho said he had also drawn a line under the [USN:L6N41L0VM TEXT:"changing-room fight "]between Aurelien Tchouameni and Federico Valverde late last season, saying both players had convinced him there was no need for peace talks. "With them, I've decided to start from scratch," Mourinho said. "Ever since Tchouameni arrived, I've been keeping a close eye on things and haven't felt the need to say anything. I’ve observed from afar and all I saw was complete normality. What I saw was peace, friendship, companionship. As if nothing have happened."

item.title: As sustainable funds struggle, give investors a direct way to back the custodians of nature
item.description: Like many people of my generation, I grew up believing that changing the world was possible. Pop songs like We Are the World, Heal the World, and Man in the Mirror taught us that individuals could make a difference. Cartoons like Captain Planet left many of us convinced that protecting the environment was one of the noblest causes we could pursue.
item.dc:creator: Ricardo Narvaez
item.content:encoded: Like many people of my generation, I grew up believing that changing the world was possible. Pop songs like We Are the World, Heal the World, and Man in the Mirror taught us that individuals could make a difference. Cartoons like Captain Planet left many of us convinced that protecting the environment was one of the noblest causes we could pursue. Years later, that desire led me into climate finance. I believed I was joining an industry that existed to help prevent one of humanity's greatest challenges: climate change. I felt fortunate to be contributing, even if only with a small grain of sand, to a much larger effort. Then an event at London Climate Action Week in June prompted me to look at my profession in a new way. During a panel discussion at Nature4Climate's Nature Hub, Lori Melton, a forest landowner from Arkansas, explained what prompted her to participate in a carbon credit programme arranged by a local forest-carbon developer, NativState , whose president, Stuart Allen, was also on the panel. Lori still owns the forestland her father left her. It is more than a property; it is a family legacy. Every year, developers approach her with offers worth six and even seven figures. Selling would undoubtedly ease many of her family's financial pressures. However, income from NativState’s forest carbon programme has given her financial breathing room that she doesn't have to sell what she values most. For years, I've thought of climate finance as an avenue for helping nature. Lori reminded me that while our efforts help the planet, what they really do is help people. Climate finance provides a service to people who already value nature but face economic pressures that may force them to push that value aside. In Lori's case, climate finance bought her the freedom to keep her land and preserve her father’s legacy. Land in Arkansas that is being managed by forest-carbon developer NativState. Handout via REUTERS Her story reminded me of Mark Manson's The Subtle Art of Not Giving a F*ck. Beneath its provocative title lies a simple but powerful idea: our lives are defined not by what happens to us, but by what we choose to value. Lori clearly values her family's heritage more than maximising her bank account. But that raises an uncomfortable question for the rest of us: what do we value? Most investors understandably prioritise financial returns. Indeed, recent years have shown that many are unwilling to sacrifice performance for sustainability objectives, helping drive a retreat from ESG-labelled products. But do we really believe that earning an additional 0.25% or 0.5% on an investment portfolio is more valuable than healthy forests, clean rivers, thriving biodiversity and the communities that protect them? Today, sustainable investing largely asks investors to avoid harm or identify companies with lower environmental risks. Perhaps the next evolution is something more direct: allowing people to intentionally express their values through their investments. Imagine opening your investment account or pension statement and seeing a simple question: "Would you like to allocate 0.5% or 1% of your investment returns toward verified forest conservation, high-quality carbon credits or other nature-positive initiatives?" For most investors, such a contribution would barely affect long-term returns. Collectively, however, those small choices could generate billions of dollars each year. More importantly, they could provide thousands of land stewards, from Arkansas to the Amazon, with exactly what Lori described: enough financial flexibility to choose conservation over conversion. Climate finance often talks about mobilising capital. Perhaps we should also be talking about mobilising values. The future of nature conservation will not be secured solely by regulations, philanthropy or increasingly sophisticated financial engineering. It will also depend on whether ordinary investors are given opportunities to align their money with what they genuinely care about. After all, every investment reflects a set of values, whether we acknowledge it or not. Lori's story is not really about carbon markets. It is not even about forestry. It is about freedom. The freedom to hold on to what matters most. If climate finance can provide that freedom, not just to one landowner in Arkansas, but to millions of farmers, Indigenous communities and forest owners around the world, safeguarding nature may become not an act of sacrifice, but simply the most rational expression of who we are.

item.title: Bangladesh PM Rahman likely to visit India from August 23-25, Indian newspaper reports
item.description: Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman is likely to visit India from August 23 to 25, the Indian Express newspaper reported on Friday, his first trip to the country since taking office in February.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman is likely to visit India from August 23 to 25, the Indian Express newspaper reported on Friday, his first trip to the country since taking office in February. The visit comes amid efforts by the South Asian neighbours to repair ties strained by the 2024 ouster of former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, whom Dhaka has asked New Delhi to extradite. The Bangladeshi and Indian foreign ministries did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Rahman's six-month old government has sought good relations with India since coming to power and the countries have been talking for weeks over his possible visit to New Delhi. Bangladesh, however, signalled last week that a more [USN:L4N44D021 TEXT:"favourable diplomatic environment"] was needed for the trip, days after Hasina addressed a media interaction in a move condemned by Dhaka. Forced to flee Bangladesh following violent protests against her government, Hasina was sentenced to death in absentia in November for ordering a deadly crackdown on the student-led uprising. She has denied the charges, dismissing them as politically motivated, and told reporters that she [USN:L1N4420TR TEXT:"would return"] to her country in December.

item.title: UBS Global Wealth Management lifts S&P 500 year-end target to 8,100
item.description: UBS Global Wealth Management raised its year-end target for the S&P 500 index to 8,100, citing a stronger earnings outlook and confidence in sustained profit growth through next year.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: UBS Global Wealth Management raised its year-end target for the S&P 500 index (.SPX) to 8,100, citing a stronger earnings outlook and confidence in sustained profit growth through next year. The wealth management arm of UBS Bank (UBSG.S) , UBS Global Wealth Management is the newest addition to a [USN:L4N4480E6 TEXT:"growing chorus"] of global research firms forecasting the S&P 500 will be above 8,000 by the end of 2026. The new target implies a roughly 6% upside from Thursday's close of 7,641.16 points. UBS, which maintained its "attractive" view on U.S. equities, said the "three pillars" supporting the bull market — resilient economic growth, supportive monetary policy and AI adoption — were firmly in place. "While AI-related companies remain key contributors, recent performance has also been supported by improving conditions in more cyclical parts of the economy," it said in a note dated Thursday. The wealth management unit raised its forecasts for S&P 500 earnings per share to $350 in 2026 and $400 in 2027, from its previous estimates of $335 and $375, respectively. UBS also raised its 2027 mid-year index target to 8,400 from 8,200.

item.title: Indonesia prioritises Kalimantan region as wildfire hotspots rise
item.description: Indonesia will tackle wildfires in Kalimantan as a matter of priority, the country's disaster agency said on Friday after identifying a rise in hotspots in the region, which shares a border with Malaysia on the island of Borneo.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Indonesia will tackle wildfires in Kalimantan as a matter of priority, the country's disaster agency said on Friday after identifying a rise in hotspots in the region, which shares a border with Malaysia on the island of Borneo. Here are more details: The government's wildfire monitoring website, Sipongi Kemenhut, recorded 1,250 hotspots this week, up from 1,187 a week earlier, with more than 900 detected in Kalimantan alone. Some regencies in the region are already suffering unhealthy air quality levels. The disaster agency, known as BNPB, said it has deployed helicopters to conduct patrols, seed clouds and drop water bombs to contain the fires in six priority provinces: Riau, Jambi, South Sumatra, South Kalimantan, Central Kalimantan and West Kalimantan. Nearly 13,000 personnel have been assigned to the three provinces in Kalimantan to carry out patrols and ground firefighting operations. A total of 3,736 hotspots have been detected so far in August, compared with 758 in July, although the daily hotspot numbers have fallen sharply in recent days. "The decline (in hotspot figures) is a positive development in forest and land fire monitoring. However, it does not indicate that all the fires have been extinguished or that the risk of forest and land fires has ended," the Indonesian forestry ministry said in a separate statement on Friday. Indonesia's weather agency expects El Niño to last into [USN:L4N43W0E1 TEXT:"early 2027"], with the critical period for forest and land fires expected to last from August to September. Forestry ministry data [USN:L6N44F0KY TEXT:"showed"] that 202,004 hectares (499,162 acres) of land had been hit by wildfire from January to July, surging from 107,465 hectares burned from January to June. Last week, more than [USN:L6N4490MY TEXT:"100 schools"] were closed in Malaysia's Sarawak state to protect children from worsening haze caused by forest fires in neighbouring Indonesia, Malaysia's national news agency reported. Separately, the environment ministry said it has inspected fires within the concession area of the palm oil company, PT Bintang Harapan Palma, in South Sumatra's Ogan Komering Ilir regency after identifying a number of hotspots.

item.title: Bolsa de Xangai fecha estável; Hong Kong sobe com expectativas de estímulo fiscal
item.description: O índice de referência da bolsa de Xangai fechou praticamente inalterado nesta sexta-feira, enquanto as ações de Hong Kong registraram uma leve alta, já que os investidores mantinham a esperança de mais apoio fiscal no país, mesmo enquanto aguardavam um novo catalisador dos mercados internacionais após uma recente onda de vendas de títulos globais.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O índice de referência da bolsa de Xangai fechou praticamente inalterado nesta sexta-feira, enquanto as ações de Hong Kong registraram uma leve alta, já que os investidores mantinham a esperança de mais apoio fiscal no país, mesmo enquanto aguardavam um novo catalisador dos mercados internacionais após uma recente onda de vendas de títulos globais. No fechamento, o índice de Xangai (.SSEC) fechou praticamente estável em 3.905 pontos, enquanto o índice CSI300 (.CSI300) , que reúne as maiores companhias listadas em Xangai e Shenzhen, avançou 0,6%. Na semana, o SSEC recuou 0,6%, enquanto o CSI300 caiu 1%. Em Hong Kong, o índice de referência Hang Seng (.HSI) avançou 1,2%, enquanto as ações do setor de tecnologia da cidade (.HTECH) registraram alta de 1,4%. O índice ChiNext Composite (.CNT) , da bolsa para startups, subiu 1,4%, e o índice STAR50 de Xangai (.STAR50) , focado em tecnologia, fechou estável. “A China ainda está tendo dificuldades para ganhar impulso”, afirmou Wee Khoon Chong, estrategista macroeconômico da região Ásia-Pacífico do BNY. “O Índice Composto de Xangai e o STAR50 permaneceram estáveis, apesar dos comentários do Ministério das Finanças de que um apoio fiscal adicional pode ser considerado no segundo semestre do ano. A reação moderada sugere que as expectativas em relação às políticas já estão elevadas, e os investidores ainda querem evidências mais claras de uma demanda interna mais forte antes de assumir riscos.” A China implementará medidas adicionais de política fiscal em resposta aos desdobramentos econômicos, afirmou na sexta-feira o vice-ministro das Finanças, Liao Min, em meio à desaceleração do crescimento na segunda maior economia do mundo. Uma série de dados de julho, que vão da produção industrial e vendas no varejo até os empréstimos, mostrou que a segunda maior economia do mundo enfrenta uma demanda interna persistentemente fraca. As ações do setor de metais não ferrosos estiveram entre as que mais valorizaram, com um subíndice (.CSI000811) subindo 2,7%, refletindo os preços mais altos do ouro em função da desvalorização do dólar e da iniciativa de recompra de títulos do Treasury dos EUA. Os participantes do mercado logo voltarão sua atenção para o discurso do chair do Federal Reserve, Kevin Warsh, no simpósio do banco central em Jackson Hole na próxima semana, em busca de pistas sobre como ele planeja lidar com a inflação ainda elevada. A recompra surpresa de títulos pelo departamento do Tesouro dos EUA não conseguiu acalmar as preocupações persistentes com a inflação e o aumento da dívida pública. . Em TÓQUIO, o índice Nikkei (.N225) recuou 0,30%, a 66.016 pontos. . Em HONG KONG, o índice HANG SENG (.HSI) subiu 1,21%, a 26.009 pontos. . Em XANGAI, o índice SSEC (.SSEC) ganhou 0,04%, a 3.905 pontos. . O índice CSI300 (.CSI300) , que reúne as maiores companhias listadas em XANGAI e SHENZHEN, avançou 0,57%, a 4.618 pontos. . Em SEUL, o índice KOSPI (.KS11) teve valorização de 0,88%, a 6.912 pontos. . Em TAIWAN, o índice TAIEX (.TWII) registrou alta de 0,65%, a 45.224 pontos. . Em CINGAPURA, o índice STRAITS TIMES (.STI) valorizou-se 0,30%, a 5.688 pontos. . Em SYDNEY, o índice S&P/ASX 200 (.AXJO) recuou 0,27%, a 9.058 pontos. (Reportagem da Redação de Xangai)

item.title: Zona euro, attività economica tocca massimi da novembre
item.description: Ad agosto l’attività economica della zona euro ha accelerato al ritmo più sostenuto dell’anno, supportata dall’aumento dei nuovi ordini — in particolare nel settore manifatturiero — e dalla ripresa della crescita delle esportazioni. L’indagine segnala inoltre un allentamento delle pressioni sui prezzi.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Ad agosto l’attività economica della zona euro ha accelerato al ritmo più sostenuto dell’anno, supportata dall’aumento dei nuovi ordini — in particolare nel settore manifatturiero — e dalla ripresa della crescita delle esportazioni. L’indagine segnala inoltre un allentamento delle pressioni sui prezzi. Ciò suggerisce che in questo trimestre l’economia sia stata resiliente nonostante il conflitto in Medio Oriente, dopo aver registrato un’espansione dello 0,4% nel secondo trimestre. L'indice Pmi composito S&P Global Flash per la zona euro è salito a 52,1 dal 52,0 di luglio, toccando il livello più alto da novembre e battendo le previsioni di un sondaggio Reuters che indicavano 51,7. Sopra la soglia di 50,0 l'indice segnala espansione dell'attività. I dati definitivi si sono rivelati migliori rispetto ai dati preliminari degli ultimi cinque mesi. I nuovi ordini, un indicatore chiave della domanda, hanno registrato la crescita più significativa degli ultimi 40 mesi, mentre gli ordini all’esportazione, compreso il commercio all’interno della zona euro, sono aumentati per la prima volta dall’invasione russa dell’Ucraina nel febbraio 2022. Il Pmi manifatturiero è salito a 52,8 da 51,9, ai massimi degli ultimi quattro anni e oltre la stima del 51,8. La crescita della produzione ha toccato massimo degli ultimi 54 mesi. L’attività nel settore dei servizi si è mantenuta stabile dopo il rimbalzo di luglio, con il Pmi rimasto invariato a 51,7, smentendo le previsioni di un rallentamento. L’occupazione complessiva è cresciuta per la prima volta quest’anno, poiché le aziende manifatturiere hanno ripreso ad assumere dopo oltre tre anni, mentre l’occupazione nel settore dei servizi è aumentata al ritmo più sostenuto degli ultimi otto mesi. Le pressioni sui prezzi, pur restando elevate, hanno continuato ad attenuarsi, con la crescita dei costi dei fattori di produzione ai minimi degli ultimi sei mesi e l’inflazione dei prezzi alla produzione a quelli degli ultimi cinque. Secondo un sondaggio Reuters della scorsa settimana, la Banca centrale europea dovrebbe procedere il mese prossimo al secondo rialzo dei tassi dell'anno. Nonostante il quadro incoraggiante, le imprese si sono mostrate meno ottimiste sulle prospettive per l'anno prossimo, con la fiducia che resta al di sotto della media storica della serie.

item.title: Stabili verso calo settimanale, prezzi greggio e rendimenti restano elevati
item.description: L'azionario europeo registra variazioni marginali, avviandosi verso un calo settimanale, penalizzato dalle pressioni sui mercati obbligazionari globali, mentre lo stallo diplomatico nel Golfo alimenta il rialzo del greggio e ravviva i timori inflazionistici.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: L'azionario europeo registra variazioni marginali, avviandosi verso un calo settimanale, penalizzato dalle pressioni sui mercati obbligazionari globali, mentre lo stallo diplomatico nel Golfo alimenta il rialzo del greggio e ravviva i timori inflazionistici. ** L'indice paneuropeo Stoxx 600 (.STOXX) guadagna lo 0,14% a 651,728 punti alle 9.45, apprestandosi verso il secondo calo settimanale consecutivo. ** I rendimenti dei titoli del Tesoro statunitense riprendono la corsa al rialzo dopo la breve tregua seguita dall'intervento di mercoledì a sostegno di un mercato obbligazionario già sotto pressione. ** Il movimento si registra nonostante il segretario al Tesoro statunitense Scott Bessent abbia annunciato la possibilità di incrementare i riacquisti di titoli di Stato e abbia aperto alla prospettiva di un consolidamento fiscale. ** Il settore delle industrie estrattive (.SXPP) guida i rialzi, salendo dell’1,3% trainato dalla debolezza del dollaro, che sostiene i prezzi dell'oro. ** Bessent torna al centro dell'attenzione ribadendo il sostegno del presidente Donald Trump a una strategia di pressione economica sull'Iran: gli Stati Uniti sarebbero pronti a imporre "le sanzioni più severe della storia" nei confronti di Teheran. ** Queste minacce frenano ulteriormente l’ottimismo su un accordo per la riapertura completa dello Stretto di Hormuz, spingendo il Brent al massimo mensile di 94,71 dollari prima delle prese di profitto.
